# dsh-crew

> A DeepSeek Harness (dsh) plugin that seats other coding agents as live
> terminal panes beside dsh: each crew member is a real PTY running its own
> CLI in the session's workspace, streamed to a split view in the Web UI.
> The human watches and can take the keyboard; the dsh agent gets five
> tools to seat crew, hand them work, and read their screens.

npm: `@dshworks/dsh-crew` (scoped; the bundle patch's `name` must match it).
Install: `dsh plugin --profile web add @dshworks/dsh-crew`.

## What it is for

The harness already ships `subagent-claude-code` and `subagent-codex`.
Those are opaque by contract: one task in, one final sentence out, no
progress stream, no human interaction path, and the model-facing terminal
tool documents "no TUI". dsh-crew is the other half — the delegation and
the observation are the same terminal.

## The two halves

- **Host** (`@dshworks/dsh-crew`, `lib/index.js`). Injects `subprocess`
  and `webServer`; injects `tools` optionally. Mounts `POST
  /dsh-crew/rpc` (ops: `roster`, `list`, `spawn`, `attach`, `input`,
  `signal`, `peek`, `close`) and a WebSocket upgrade at
  `/dsh-crew/attach?token=…`. Config: `agents`, `trustedHosts`, `cols`
  (100), `rows` (30), `scrollbackBytes` (262144), `maxPanesPerSession`
  (6), `graceMs` (3000), `tools` (true).
- **Web UI** (`dist/client.js`, built from `src/client/`). Discovered from
  package.json's `dsh.client` block, not from the bundle patch. Adds a
  **Crew** tab beside Chat and Trajectory: a seat bar plus one xterm.js
  pane per seated agent.

## The five tools

`crew_list` (roster + this session's panes), `crew_seat(agent)` (returns
`paneId` and the first settled screen), `crew_send(pane, message,
timeoutSeconds=180, max 900)` (types the text, presses Enter, waits for
the screen to go quiet), `crew_peek(pane, lines?)`, `crew_dismiss(pane)`.
A tool call may only touch panes belonging to its own session.

## Built-in roster

`claude` → `claude`, `codex` → `codex`, `dsh` → `dsh`, each spawned in its
interactive form (no prompt argument). A roster entry is data: `agents`
rows override built-ins by `id` field-by-field, or append new ones.
`enabled: false` removes one. Availability is resolved against PATH
*before* any spawn so a button can be disabled with the reason on it.

## Facts that are easy to get wrong

- **The workspace never comes from request data.** It is read from the
  named dsh session's `header.cwd`. An unresolvable session is refused,
  not defaulted to the server's cwd — defaulting would hand an agent write
  access to wherever dsh was launched, on an unrecognized id alone.
- **`TERM` must be overridden per pane.** The harness server usually runs
  from a non-interactive shell, so ambient `TERM=dumb` is inherited by the
  subprocess seam, and a coding CLI reading `dumb` disables colour and
  cursor addressing. Panes declare `xterm-256color` + `truecolor`.
- **The host runs a headless xterm mirror** (`lib/screen.js`) over the same
  bytes the browser gets. `crew_peek` returns the rendered grid; the raw
  byte stream is escape sequences and repaints, and stripping escapes
  yields overlapping fragments, not a screen. Always `await drain()`
  before `read()` — xterm's `write` is async by contract.
- **`crew_send` settles rather than returning immediately.** A CLI that has
  not begun rendering its reply is momentarily as quiet as one that
  finished, so the quiet window (3s) has to outlast that gap.
- **The control route requires `application/json`.** This is a security
  control, not a formality: a cross-site "simple" request cannot set it.
- **The attach token is single-use, 30s TTL**, minted only by the
  fence-passing control route.
- **A malformed `trustedHosts` entry throws at load**, because
  `user@evil.example` would otherwise silently grant `evil.example`.
- **`dist/client.js` is committed** and its module-loader `id` must equal
  the package name — a different id registers a factory nobody resolves
  and the client half silently never materializes, with no error.
- **The bundler emits IIFE, not CJS.** esbuild's CJS output tags exports
  with `__esModule`, which the Loader reads as an ES module and then looks
  for a default export that is not there. `react` stays external — two
  React copies in one document break hooks.
- **Nothing writes the session log.** Raw terminal bytes are not
  conversation state.

## Files

`lib/index.js` (routes, config, dispatch), `lib/panes.js` (PTY registry,
scrollback ring, attach tokens), `lib/roster.js` (crew data + PATH
resolution), `lib/screen.js` (headless emulator mirror), `lib/tools.js`
(the five tools + settle watcher), `lib/trust.js` (the request fence),
`src/client/` (Web UI source), `scripts/build-client.mjs` (bundler,
`--check` verifies freshness), `tests/host.spec.mjs` (15 tests against
real PTYs and sockets).
